speaker: Kai
text: Bigger than you look. Of course you are.
The cave narrows, then turns, then — doesn't end. Cold air moving across his face, where no air should move.

speaker: Kai
text: A draft. Deep in a hill. …Drafts mean openings.

A wall that is not a wall: worked stone, seamless, old past counting. And as he stands there — runes surface. Faint lines waking one after another, tracing a slow ring, like a crown being drawn in light. Like something noticing him.
The wall opens. Not like stone breaking. Like a door being answered.
It does not open because he was clever. It opens because of who is standing in front of it.
Beyond: a round chamber no torch has lit in centuries — lit anyway. In the center, a stone hangs in the air. Unsupported. Ringed with slow-turning runes.
Its light is not firelight. Not daylight. It is warm the way a window is warm at night — when you're coming home late, and someone left the lamp burning for you.
He steps closer. Hand half-raised. Stops an inch away.

speaker: Kai
text: This is a bad idea. This is — *such* a bad idea.
But the light was warm, and the dark behind him was cold, and he had come much too far to not know.
A sound like a bell, the size of the sky.

Light stands up out of the hill in a column — seen from Oakstead's square, from the garrison tower, from further away than anyone will ever admit. The ground around the cave scorches in a perfect ring.
Somewhere very far away, something that had been searching for a long, long time… lifted its head.
